summary: n8n-nodes-task-runner exfiltrates AWS/ECS credentials to webhook.site on import
details: Package presents itself as an n8n community node but ships a trivial stub (MyNode.js) while its declared main (index.js) executes credential-theft code at require time. On import, recon() enumerates AWS_/ECS_ environment variables, fetches ECS task metadata from ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4, retrieves IAM credentials from the ECS credentials endpoint at 169.254.170.2 via AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI, and POSTs the collected data to a hardcoded webhook.site URL. index.js additionally writes a SigV4 signer to /tmp/.aws_call.py and shells out via python3 to invoke STS GetCallerIdentity, S3 ListBuckets, EC2 DescribeRegions, and EKS ListClusters using the stolen task-role credentials, with responses exfiltrated to the same webhook. The n8n-node cover story targets AWS-hosted n8n installations where importing the module yields access to task-role cloud identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
